text: Chainlink Price Feeds are independent node operators fetching a price from multiple sources, aggregated into one published value — exactly Lesson 17's real fix, already built.
Reading a feed is a read-only call against AggregatorV3Interface. The feed address is hardcoded, and latestRoundData returns five values, though a simple consumer usually only needs the answer.
This isn't theoretical. Here's that exact contract in Remix, selecting a Solidity compiler version that matches the pragma.
Then compiling it, successfully, against the real AggregatorV3Interface import.
Deploying needs a real wallet connection — Remix's Injected Provider hands signing off to MetaMask instead of Remix's own test accounts.
With the contract selected and a wallet connected, Deploy sends an actual transaction onto the testnet.
The connected wallet prompts to confirm, gas fee and all — same as any other on-chain transaction.
Once deployed, calling getChainlinkDataFeedLatestAnswer returns a live value straight from the feed, scaled by the feed's decimals.
Price Feeds answer what's the current value of X. Lesson 19 covers Chainlink Automation and Functions, and an important update on where both stand today.
